question.problem:
| **Price per Bag, in $$$ ($x$)** | $2$ | $3$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Number of Bags Sold ($y$)** | $28$ | $20$ | $24$ | $16$ |

The table above shows the results of a survey conducted in four fast food outlets. It shows data on the number of bags of onion rings sold daily and the price per bag. Calculate the covariance of the data sets.
question.worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x=\{{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}\}$ and $y=\{{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}\}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

First, we need to compute the means:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (2+3+3+4) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 12 \\  & =3 \\ \overset{―}{y} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (28+20+24+16) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 88 \\  & =22\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(2\,-\,3)(28\,-\,22)+(3\,-\,3)(20\,-\,22)+(3\,-\,3)(24\,-\,22)+(4\,-\,3)(16\,-\,22)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-1)(6)+(0)(-2)+(0)(2)+(1)(-6)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[-6+0+0+(-6)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (-12) \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$
